# Data-quality issue table (generated by scripts/01_eda.py, effects updated by scripts/02_validation_design.py)

| # | issue | how detected | rows affected | fix | effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Duplicate rows / ids | duplicated(load_id); duplicated(all cols except id) | 0 | none needed | none (0 duplicates in train; 0 in validation) |
| 2 | City / equipment spelling | 64 distinct cities, 3 equipment values, whitespace check | 0 | none needed | values are already canonical (Dry Van/Flatbed/Reefer) |
| 3 | Negative weights (sign errors) | weight < 0; /weight/ mean/quantiles identical to positive rows (31,724 vs 31,417) | 292 train, 145 validation | abs(weight) | baseline MAE 71.0->69.0 and RMSE 101.1->96.1 when weight is abs() instead of raw (clean eval); dropping weight entirely gives MAE 82.3 |
| 4 | Weight censored at 47,500 lb | mass point at /weight/ == 47,500 | 1204 train, 301 validation | keep (legal max load); optional is_capped flag | documented; no row removed |
| 5 | Null weight | isna(); rate by month/equipment/date; mean rate null vs not-null | 300 train (0.62%), 165 validation | median impute (by equipment) + was_missing flag, or native NaN for GBMs | missingness looks random (month rate 0.004-0.008, mean rate 2351 vs 2374) |
| 6 | Null market_index | isna(); market_index is a daily series (within-date sd 0.025 vs between-date sd 0.167) | 374 train (0.78%), 249 validation | fill with same-date median of the other loads (every date has observed values) | market_index is the strongest feature: baseline MAE 101.9->69.0 with it; date-median fill keeps it available for all rows |
| 7 | Corrupted posted_rate labels (x0.17-0.47 or x2.1-5.3) | /log-residual/ > 10 robust sigma (0.046) from structural fit (equipment, log-dist, market_index); clean residual is tight, 0 rows between 0.3-0.5 and only a few 0.5-0.8; flag rate is flat across equipment/month/distance | 677 train (1.41%): 340 high, 337 low | drop from training and from CV/holdout scoring (also report holdout on all rows); never 'predict' them | CV folds Mar-Aug, log-linear baseline: removing them from TRAINING changes MAE 120.3->118.2, RMSE 602.4->601.4 (small, the log fit is robust); but they dominate any error metric: RMSE 601 on all eval rows vs 96 on clean rows (MAE 118 vs 69). Irreducible if validation labels contain the same corruption; matters a lot for squared-error GBMs trained on raw rate. |
| 8 | Coordinates: per-row deviation from city median | nunique(lat,lon) per city; /train-val/ coord diff for shared cities | 0 | use row coordinates (== city medians); Lexington/Fort Wayne taken from train city medians | max nunique per city = 1; max train-vs-val diff = 0.0e+00 |
| 9 | Coordinates are synthetic / clipped | Baltimore lon -72.7 etc. do not match real geography; lat in [28.36,44.30], lon in [-121.70,-69.50]; Laredo (validation only) lat 25.5 | all rows | treat lat/lon as city identifiers in a synthetic plane; do not use external geography | haversine*1.18 ~ distance (corr 0.9995), so coordinates and distance agree internally |
| 10 | distance vs haversine mismatch | ratio = distance/haversine: median 1.18, p1 1.13, p99 1.404; ratio>1.6 are only short hauls | 111 train ratio>1.6 (median distance 84 mi) | keep; explained by 70-mile floor on distance + noise on very short lanes | no rows removed; haversine used only as a cross-check/feature |
| 11 | Row-level distance noise within a lane | same pickup/delivery has 10 distinct distances (median sd 15.9 mi) | most lanes | use row distance plus lane-mean distance as separate features | Lexington->Fort Wayne seen in train: 32 rows, mean 363.7 mi vs fixed 360 |
| 12 | Cold-start cities in validation | set(val cities) - set(train cities) | 1447 validation rows (12.1%): Allentown, Charlotte, Chicago, Jackson, Knoxville, Laredo, Norfolk, San Diego | no city-ID/target-encoding as sole signal; rely on distance, equipment, coordinates, market_index; evaluate with the cold-start holdout | Laredo lat 25.5 lies outside train lat range (28.36-44.30): tree models will extrapolate flat |
| 13 | Monthly trend | monthly median rate-per-mile vs mean market_index (clean rows) | all | market_index is the carrier of trend; no calendar-time feature (Nov/Dec are out of range) | rpm 2.03-2.25 tracks market_index 0.89-1.30; corr(log-rate residual after equipment+distance, market_index)=0.44 |
| 14 | Day-of-week effect | median rpm by weekday (clean rows) | all | weak; optional weekday feature | spread 2.1% of mean rpm |
| 15 | quote_signal is NOT a near-proxy of the target but is unstable | corr with equipment+distance residual is small; its slope on log-rate flips sign by month (+0.06 in high-mean months, -0.05 in low-mean months) - see quote_signal_by_month.csv | all | use with caution: test in CV with/without; do not rely on it for Nov/Dec | overall corr with residual 0.067 (market_index: 0.439); monthly slope +-0.04-0.06 x qs sd 0.26 = at most ~+-1.6% of rate |
| 16 | Market regime shift (validation market_index) | validation mean 0.927 (range 0.72-1.10) vs train 1.083 (0.68-1.47); train share below val mean | 12000 validation rows | model market_index monotonically/log-linearly; rely on the Jan/Aug-Oct (low-index) months for fit quality; Dec market_index filled from validation features per date | 0% of validation market_index outside train range; quote_signal outside-range 0.00% |
| 17 | Train-vs-validation covariate shift (adversarial validation) | LightGBM classifier train(0) vs validation(1), date excluded: AUC=0.876 (all), 0.755 (no market_index), 0.727 (no market_index/geo) | all validation rows | keep features that are stable (distance, equipment, weight); handle market_index via regime-robust modelling; use time-based CV that mimics the shift | control: Sep-Oct vs Jan-Aug inside train AUC=0.925 |
